discrepancies: Prior lead (research/launch-gap/part_2026.json) linked the complaint to 'Alkemi' only by inference and listed Yoink as copying the DHL attacker; the DHL attack tx 0xa17001eb is in a different pool and shares no call with Yoink's tx.
evidence_notes: incidents/alkemi-2026/replay_diff.json: 16 of 16 state-changing Alkemi calls of the reverted tx 0x726bd90c equal Yoink's first 16 (supply 1 WBTC, supply 2.5 ETH, 7x borrow 2 ETH + liquidateBorrow(self) 2.002 ETH); Yoink adds 2 withdraws.

Fork replay (local anvil, block 24627180 state): the reverted tx at its own 14,974,454 gas limit reverts with exactly the on-chain gas used (14,344,401); with a 30M limit it succeeds and sends 29,884,523 sat WBTC to the attacker EOA = the amount Yoink swapped.

The message sender's own attack tx replayed on state after block 24627180 (traceCall) moves all 29,980,756 sat WBTC to 0x460eba8f; on the real state after Yoink it moves 55,199. Its calls share nothing with Yoink's.
Alkemi balances (end of block): WBTC 0.29980756 until 24627180, 0.00055199 after 24627181, 0 after 24627182; ETH vault 44.17125 before 24626979, 0.7173 after, 0 from 24627055.
Our call-level comparison for c0ffeebabe.eth transactions is withheld by policy; the public traces can be compared by anyone.
verdict_reason: Alkemi Earn's self-liquidation bug (BlockSec) was used on two pools. The 'attack tx' DeFiHackLabs lists (0xa17001eb, block 24626979, +43.45395 ETH, ETH vault) is not what Yoink touched. Yoink's tx 0x7acef470 (block 24627181 idx 0) hits the WBTC pool and contains the same 16 state-changing Alkemi calls (+2 withdraws) as the deploy+attack tx 0x726bd90c of EOA 0x46c403e3, which was mined one block earlier (24627180 idx 226) and reverted out of gas at its 14,974,454 gas limit. A fork replay of that tx at 30M gas succeeds and pays the attacker exactly the 29,884,523 sat WBTC Yoink swapped. So Yoink retried a failed, already-mined tx; nothing of that actor's was pending. The on-chain complainant 0x8366d87b ('Why did you leak my attack transaction to yoink?', block 24627239) is a third party: its program differs (0 shared calls), its attack tx landed in 24627185 after Yoink's and found the pool empty. A traceCall of its tx on the pre-Yoink state would have taken the whole 29,980,756 sat, so Yoink did take what it was about to drain, but the leak itself is neither shown nor refuted (none of the 15 relevant txs is in mempool-dumpster although 55-63% of other txs in those blocks are). Yoink paid 10.2256 ETH coinbase (999 per mille), builder refunded 9.19 ETH, net about 9.20 ETH, no return found.
evidence_strength_basis: Call-sequence diff of both traces (16/16 identical), block positions, fork replays of both rivals' txs, relay bids (271) and balances at each block are saved. Unknowns: what triggered Yoink (its tx and every rival tx are absent from the mempool archive) and whether the complainant's tx was visible to it; no direct transfer between 0x46c403e3 and 0x8366d87b was found in their tx lists, but a shared operator is not excluded.

detection_method: not measurable: no pre-inclusion mempool first-seen of the trigger tx

Its deploy tx (0x8e7b711e, block 19287269) was first seen earlier, 02:16:22.769Z (1708654582769 ms). Winner Ty For The Block 91.0383 ETH at -587 ms, a 3-tx block: the bot tx plus two payouts from the builder's fee recipient (366.5069 ETH to the Blueberry multisig = 80.1% of the 457.5473 ETH coinbase payment, 91.0383 ETH to the proposer). Bid contents are not public; that these bids carry the bot tx is inferred from value level and the winning block contents.

Call diff (incidents/neemo-2025/call_diff.json): bot's victim-side subtree (6 calls: proxy -> delegatecall impl -> weETH.balanceOf -> weETH.transfer, plus delegatecalls into weETH's implementation) vs. the key-holder EOA calling 03b79c24(itself) on a local anvil fork at block 22855568: identical call sequence, 2 of 6 calls byte-identical, 4 differ only in the 20-byte recipient argument; both move 106.929468097270451433 weETH.

Local-fork replay (attacker_replay_local_fork.json, nothing broadcast): the bot's exact calldata reproduces the mainnet gas (137,752) and empties the proxy; a fresh unrelated address can do the same (no access control); the thief's real follow-up selectors 0x53474b2c / 0x97e44edc do not move weETH; a thief call to 0x03b79c24 after the bot moves 0 weETH.

Calls to the proxy in blocks 22855560-22862000 (trace_filter incl. reverted): upgrade, bot drain, 0x53474b2c (22855612), 0x97e44edc (22855836) - nothing else. Later: 0x67a28887 calls 0x97e44edc (2026-07-17), 0x8c8aaebd calls 0x03b79c24 (2026-09-28, moved 0).

Thief-side proceeds are separate: 176.57 ETH = 12.27 (key-holder EOA) + 160.9 + 3.4 (0x198b2c4e) to collection address 0x4ec65e4d, then 176.4 ETH into Tornado Router; the ETH arrived via contracts such as 0x5c7bcd6e (implementation named Ethereum_SpokePool). Not part of the bot's take.

Not c0ffeebabe and not Yoink. No on-chain link to the key holder or the collection address was found. Our call-level comparison for c0ffeebabe.eth transactions is withheld by policy; the public traces can be compared by anyone.

name: TaoPad
race_type_reason: The counterparty is the TaoPad operator (not a hacker). Its tx failed on chain (out of gas, block 19226482); Yoink replayed the same victim-protocol call sequence 21 blocks / 252 s later with a higher gas limit. Nothing was pending in between and no other tx called the vulnerable function.
one_liner: TaoPad's own operator tx to pull the token's 29.2 ETH tax balance ran out of gas; Yoink replayed its calls 4 min later (net 26.32 ETH) and returned it all the next day after the team wrote to it.

attacker.none_reason: No hostile attacker in this event. The racing counterparty is the project's operator (below). The earlier third-party exploit of the TPAD token that TaoPad mentions is outside the scope and not identified here.
